cited.quote: Since 10.11.2021, Journalists‟ Family Benefit Fund has been increased to Rs.1,25,000/- for those who have served for 5 years

rationale: C2 shows the family benefit fund amount was increased from 10.11.2021, which covers one part of the promise. No extract shows an independent commission with Labour Welfare and Police members, revision of press regulations, skills training or dispute settlement; C2 only shows a welfare board committee chaired by the Minister. So only part is implemented.

cited.quote: Subsidy assistance of 40% of the unit cost of the engine or Rs.48,000/- whichever is less is being provided
a total of 1,000 OBMs/IBEs (upto 28 HP) have been distributed to traditional fishermen under the State

rationale: C1 (2021) already shows a 40% or Rs.48,000 engine subsidy, and C2 shows the same Rs.48,000 rate for 2023-24 distribution. No extract shows an order raising the engine subsidy rate; the scheme only continued at the same level. Other subsidies (C4, C5) concern boats, not engines.

cited.quote: Orders issued for constructing a Manimandapam with full size statue for Pollan, the commander of Dheeran

rationale: C1 (policy note of 2021-12-05) reports orders issued for a Manimandapam with full size statue for Pollan at Modakurichi, Erode District, at Rs.1.82 crore. This is an official step, but no extract shows the statue erected or the work completed. C2 and C3 do not mention Pollan.

C1 and C2 are irrigation sluice and syphon works in Thirukuvalai and Nagapattinam taluks; C3 and C4 concern Chennai Metro Rail; C5 is a Gandhi statue shift for a metro station. None concerns a Thirukuvalai-Nagapattinam broad gauge rail line.

cited.quote: to compensate for their sufferings/loss ranging from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.15 Lakhs.
Special Medical Relief is available to subscribers and their dependents up to three times

rationale: C2 (Police policy note 2022-23) shows the ex-gratia range unchanged at Rs.20,000 to Rs.15 lakhs, with ad hoc payments from the relief fund. C4 describes the Police Benevolent Fund relief without any increase order. C3 and C5 concern insurance document fees and risk allowance for shorthand reporters. No order raising police medical or accident relief is shown.

cited.quote: to compensate for their sufferings/loss ranging from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.15 lakhs.
to compensate for their sufferings/loss ranging from Rs.20,000/- to Rs.15 Lakhs.

rationale: C2 (2021-22) and C3 (2022-23) state the same ex-gratia range of Rs.20,000 to Rs.15 lakhs, so no enhanced scheme is shown. C3 lists individual payments and a COVID special relief, which are ad hoc, not a scheme with an increased amount. C4 and C5 concern other employees.

C1, C3 and C5 are committees on NEET and State Education Policy chaired by retired judges, C2 is a district jail committee, and C4 describes the Human Rights Commission. None is a committee with Home and Law Secretaries, a senior woman police officer, an editor and civil society members on the issue in the promise.

cited.quote: has appointed a Special Officer to resolve all the grievance petitions received during the programme

rationale: C1 (Governor's address, 2021-06-21) says a Special Officer was appointed to resolve all petitions within 100 days and that 63,500 had been resolved so far. This is an official step with partial progress, but C1 does not show that all complaints were resolved within 100 days. C2 concerns later schemes.

cited.quote: A High Level Committee for Agriculture will be constituted at State level
Agricultural Zonal Committees will be formed consisting of officials from Departments of

rationale: C1 (budget speech) and C2 (policy note of 2021-12-29) only say the committees will be constituted or formed. No extract shows a GO forming them or recommendations to farmers against natural calamities. C3 to C5 are about other schemes.

cited.quote: A compulsory Tamil Language Paper has been introduced in all competitive examinations conducted by

rationale: The promise is to urge the Union government on exam languages. C2 shows a state step (a compulsory Tamil paper in State recruitment exams), which is a related state measure, not a formal step of advocacy to the Centre. No extract shows a resolution or letter urging the Union.

cited.quote: Nutri Farming The guidelines for implementation of this scheme will be issued separately

rationale: C5 is part of GO 162 (2021-10-25) sanctioning RKVY project proposals, including an Integrated Farming System item whose guidelines are still to be issued separately, so it is not yet operational and no subsidy is shown. C1 to C3 concern machinery subsidies, not diversified farming techniques.

cited.quote: The lumpsum amount payable under Tamil Nadu Government Servants’ Family Security Fund Scheme shall be enhanced to Rs.5,00,000/-

rationale: C5 is G.O.(Ms) No.197 dated 01.09.2021, enhancing the lumpsum payable on death in service of Government servants from Rs.3,00,000 to Rs.5,00,000. This matches the promised amounts. C1 to C4 are about other groups or schemes.

cited.quote: decided to issue the rules viz., Tamil Nadu Civil Services (Appointment on Compassionate Grounds) Rules, 2023
to amend the Tamil Nadu Civil Services (Appointment on Compassionate Grounds) Rules, 2023, to fix time frame

rationale: C2 is G.O.(Ms) No.33 of 08.03.2023 notifying the compassionate appointment rules. C4 shows the High Court later directed amendment of the rules to fix a time frame and began contempt proceedings, so the 'without delay' part was not met by the 2023 rules.

cited.quote: Aavin has undertaken all necessary efforts to expand its presence in the growing e-commerce and online retail

rationale: C2, C3 and C5 report policy-note descriptions of e-commerce sales, exports and consumer care, and C1 describes Chennai marketing infrastructure. None shows a GO, scheme or programme for technology upgrading to raise milk production or for interstate marketing.

cited.quote: At the same time the retail price at petrol bunks remain unchanged.

rationale: C1 (Finance letter, 2022-08-07) says bulk fuel prices were hiked while retail petrol bunk prices remained unchanged, and shows no cut. C2 to C5 concern CAG audit notes, GST rates and adulteration cases. No extract shows an order reducing petrol by Rs.5 or diesel by Rs.4.

C2 and C5 are the MLA constituency development scheme guidelines, which concern works funds, and C1, C3 and C4 concern police, human rights and citizen grievance portals. No extract mandates MLAs to upload the status of public complaints or demands.

C1 and C3 concern palmyrah development, C2 is an audit of oil palm plantations, C4 is coconut integrated farming and C5 is MGNREGS plantation guidelines. None mentions date palm cultivation or subsidies in Tuticorin, Vellore, Karur or Dharmapuri.

cited.quote: In the year 2021-2022, the monthly pension has been enhanced from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.4,000/-

rationale: C2 and C3 show the Village Temple Poosaris Welfare Board gives a pension of Rs.3,000, raised to Rs.4,000, only to retired poosaris aged 60 with 20 years of service. This is an existing pension for a different group, not a Rs.2,000 monthly allowance for registered priests. C4 concerns Christian priests.

cited.quote: all the 4,57,645 petitions received under the programme have been acted upon
has appointed a Special Officer to resolve all the grievance petitions received during the programme

rationale: C2 (budget speech, 2021-08-13) reports all 4,57,645 petitions acted upon and the 100-day commitment implemented; C1 records the Special Officer appointed for the 100-day disposal. The outcome is self-reported, but both extracts match the promise.

cited.quote: a Centre of Excellence for foundry in Coimbatore

rationale: C3 (budget speech 2025-26) only says TIDCO will establish a Centre of Excellence for foundry in Coimbatore, which is a future announcement and not an Indian Institute of Foundries. No extract shows a GO or other official step for the institute. Other extracts are unrelated.
